intro: Lazur is an AI assistant for architects that lives on your Mac. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask about anything on your screen, and it answers out loud. It points at controls, guides you through steps one click at a time, and types drafts and dictated notes into any app. This page covers where architects lose time, which Mac tools run natively, and how to use a voice assistant without breaking your firm's data rules.

blocks.text: How architects spend the working day

Architects lose a lot of time to work that never gets billed. A 2026 benchmark, reported in a vendor blog post, asked firms about specific non-billable tasks for the first time. Project management ranks first. Client communication and approvals come close behind. Resourcing and planning follow. Invoicing, billing, time tracking and general admin complete the list, though the post does not give their exact order. The report's publisher is not named on that page, so treat the ranking as a strong hint, not a census.

items: Project management. Ranked first among non-billable tasks in the benchmark.
Client communication and approvals. Ranked close behind project management. Often handled by email, markups and phone calls.
Resourcing and planning. Deciding who works on what, and when.
Invoicing, billing, time tracking and general admin. The rest of the list.

blocks.text: Email is the other big drain. Microsoft's 2023 data covers all knowledge workers, not architects. The heaviest 25% of them spend 8.8 hours a week on intentional email, reading and writing. No architect-specific email figure was verified for this page. A 2017 Archinect report on a survey of 9,514 US design professionals found more than half worked over 40 hours a week. The article gives no exact percentage, so use it as direction only.

Payroll and HR work is a heavier load for smaller firms. A 2020 Paychex survey of 125 US architecture firm principals, at firms with 10 to 100 staff, found 67% spend more than 10 hours a week on payroll and other HR admin. The sample is small. Paychex sells payroll and HR software, so read the result as a warning sign, not a benchmark for your office.
What an AI assistant for architects does on a Mac

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch on your Mac. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask about anything you can see. Lazur answers out loud, and it draws a circle and a label around the thing you ask about. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. That limit helps. The drawing stays in your hands, and every change is yours to make.
Lazur has seven ways to help. Each one fits a different part of the day.

items: Explain: ask what a consultant's markup means, or what a request for information is asking for.
Point: ask where a control is, and Lazur circles it on screen with a label.
Guide: ask for the steps in a task. Lazur waits for each click before it gives the next step.
Dictate: hold fn to type clean text at your cursor, such as site notes or meeting minutes.
Draft: ask for a client reply, a consultant email or a transmittal cover note.
Research: send a background job to Lazur's own Chrome tabs. It returns a summary and a report.
Everyday: timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music and opening apps, all by voice.

blocks.text: Start with the tasks you repeat. For most architects those are email replies, meeting notes and questions about a sheet on screen. Those tasks come back every day, so small savings add up. Save research jobs for the work you would otherwise do late at night, such as comparing supplier lead times.
Revit and Archicad on a Mac: what runs natively

Not every design tool runs on a Mac. Autodesk Revit has no native macOS version. Parallels says Revit runs on a Mac through a Windows virtual machine, and it cites Autodesk's recommended configuration for Revit 2026. That setup lists 16 GB of host memory and 16 GB for the Windows VM. It also needs at least 40 GB of free disk, with 100 GB recommended. Boot Camp is not available on Apple silicon. Check those numbers before you buy a Mac for Revit work.

blocks.text: Check Archicad's requirements before you update macOS. Graphisoft lists macOS 15 Sequoia, 26 and 27 as supported. It also says it does not currently recommend upgrading a primary Mac to macOS 27. The minimum is 8 GB of RAM and at least 5 GB of free NVMe disk. macOS 14.1 can install, but Graphisoft does not support it.
Email and client approvals on Mac

If your firm runs Outlook, check the version first. Microsoft's Outlook for Mac page describes a new Outlook for Mac with a Legacy Outlook switch. It says support for legacy Outlook for Mac ends in October 2026. That date has passed as of November 8, 2026, so move to the new app if you still run the old one. A 2024 Microsoft Q&A thread says Office for Mac tracks only the three newest macOS releases. That does not match the support page's macOS 10.14 line, so confirm on your own Mac.
Worked example: answering a contractor's question in Gmail

Say a contractor emails to ask whether a door swing change affects the fire rating on level 2. You need to check the sheet, confirm with the consultant and reply. Gmail runs in your browser, so open the thread in Safari or Chrome first. Then work through it with Lazur open.

items: Hold ⌥⌘ and ask: what is this contractor asking me to confirm? Lazur explains it out loud.
With the sheet on screen, ask Lazur to point at the door. A circle and a label appear.
Hold fn and dictate your note: confirm fire rating with consultant before changing the schedule. Read the text back.
Ask Lazur to draft the reply. It types the draft at your cursor. Edit the wording and the name.
Ask Lazur to remind you at 17:00 to chase the consultant. Then send the email yourself.

blocks.text: Gmail's send step stays with you. In the compose window, ⌘ Enter sends the message. Check the To line and the attachments before you press it. Once an email has gone out, no assistant can pull it back for you.

blocks.title: Check your firm's data rules first
blocks.text: Client drawings, specs and emails can be confidential. Follow your employer's rules before you share any of it with an AI tool. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is not used to train AI models. These are product facts, not a compliance certification for your firm.
PowerPoint and Photoshop for architects on Mac

Boards and client decks take more evenings than most architects expect. Lazur helps with that work without touching your files. In PowerPoint, View > Slide Master opens the master so you can fix a template once. In Photoshop, File > Export > Export As is the path to send a board at the size a client needs. Ask Lazur to walk you through each dialog, one click at a time.

Each app has its own page with the details. Read [Photoshop for architects on Mac](/for/architects/photoshop) for render passes and boards, and [PowerPoint for architects on Mac](/for/architects/powerpoint) for layouts and client decks.
Mistakes architects make with an AI assistant

items: Pasting a whole client package into an AI tool without checking your firm's rules.
Trusting a dictated note without reading it back. Dictation can mishear names, levels and dimensions.
Sending a drafted email with the wrong project name or sheet number.
Taking a code or spec answer from the assistant without checking the source document.
Expecting Lazur to change the model or the file. It guides and types. It does not edit for you.

blocks.text: Use Lazur as a second reader. The person who signs the drawing still owns the decision. Keep that line clear in your head and in your office habits.
How to measure your own admin time

Run a five-day log before you change anything. Open Notes and write the app, the task and the minutes for each block. At the end of the week, add up the email minutes and the admin minutes. A worked example: 90 minutes a day in email is 450 minutes over five days, or 7.5 hours. That sits below the 8.8 hours Microsoft reports for the heaviest 25% of workers. If your number is above 8.8, email is worth attacking first.

Do the same count for markups and project admin. Those are harder to log because they split across apps. Use the rough tally you have, not a perfect one. A rough number still shows where the week goes.
Who this fits and who should wait

Lazur fits Mac users who work across Gmail, Office, Photoshop and CAD apps. It helps most if your firm already works on Macs, or lets you use one for this work. Windows is planned, not available. If your office is Windows only, Lazur cannot run there yet. Revit users on a Mac should check the Parallels setup first, because the Windows VM takes a large share of the memory.
Costs, trial and where to start

Download Lazur from the [download page](/download). It runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. The free trial needs no credit card and starts when you first open the app. Current plans and AI action limits are on the [pricing page](/pricing). Read those before you commit, and compare the AI action limit with how often you would really use it.

If you want a quick speed check first, the [typing speed test](/tools/typing-speed-test) takes about a minute. Dictation works on the same idea. You talk into a draft instead of typing it from scratch.
What to do first this week

items: Run the five-day log in Notes. Write the app, the task and the minutes.
Pick the two tasks that repeat most. Client replies and meeting notes are common picks.
Install Lazur from the download page and open it once to start the trial.
Use it on those two tasks for a week. Note what it saved and what it got wrong.
Write your firm's rules for AI tools on one page before you paste any client file.

faq.question: Is there an AI assistant for architects that works on a Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask about anything on your screen, and it answers out loud. It points at controls, guides you through steps and types drafts. It does not click or edit for you, and it is not a plugin for any app.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Revit on a Mac?
faq.answer: Revit has no native macOS version, so most Mac users run it in Parallels with Windows. Lazur looks at what is on your screen, so it can explain or point at things in that window. It does not operate Revit for you. Check the Parallels memory and disk numbers before you buy.

faq.question: Can Lazur send emails for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur drafts and types text at your cursor. You read the draft, fix anything wrong, and send it yourself. Gmail keeps the send step with you, and so should you.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with client drawings?
faq.answer: Follow your employer's rules first. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is not used to train AI models. That is not a compliance certification, so ask your IT lead what your firm allows.

faq.question: Does it work with the new Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Lazur helps with whatever app is on screen, so it can explain or draft in Outlook. First confirm which Outlook you run. Microsoft says support for legacy Outlook for Mac ends in October 2026, so move to the new app if you still use the old one.

faq.question: Is there a Windows version?
faq.answer: Not yet. Windows is planned, not available. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.

faq.question: How do I try it without paying?
faq.answer: There is a free trial with no credit card. It starts when you first open the app. Check the pricing page for current plan details and AI action limits before you decide to keep it.
